records.topic: PG-601 overpressure on the primary circuit

turns.speaker: myer-manager
turns.text: Call convened on PG-601: {value} bar against the 3.5 bar limit. Engineer first, then compliance, then the technician.

turns.speaker: myer-engineer
turns.text: PG-601 has risen from 3.2 to {value} bar in 40 minutes. P-101 is running and TK-201 is the likely cause: a low membrane pre-charge. Isolate at V-501 and open the bypass before the relief valve lifts at 3.8 bar.

turns.speaker: myer-compliance
turns.text: TK-201's inspection plan records 3.5 bar as the circuit's limit. Plant running outside its safe limits is a risk we must control and then review under the Victorian OHS Regulations (regs 97, 98 and 121), and the inspection and the fix go in the plant record (regs 105 and 106).

turns.speaker: myer-technician
turns.text: I can reach {contactName} ({contactRole}) by {contactChannel} through the dispatch line; nobody else on shift has contact details on file.

records.resolution: Isolate the primary circuit at V-501 and open the bypass; {contactName} attends to check the TK-201 pre-charge and confirm PG-601 back below 3.5 bar.

summary.headline: PG-601 at {value} bar: isolate at V-501, duty engineer to attend
points: PG-601 rose from 3.2 to {value} bar over 40 minutes on a 3.5 bar circuit.
TK-201's membrane pre-charge is the likely cause.
Only the duty engineer has contact details on file.
decisions: Isolate the primary circuit at V-501 and open the bypass.
Duty engineer attends to check the TK-201 pre-charge.

actions.task: Text {contactName} through the dispatch line
Check TK-201 pre-charge and confirm PG-601 below 3.5 bar

records.topic: SU-201 sump rising toward the visitor walkway

turns.speaker: bristol-manager
turns.text: Call convened on SU-201: {value} % and rising, overflow onto W-1201 in about {minutes} minutes. Engineer first.

turns.speaker: bristol-engineer
turns.text: SU-201 is at {value} % and climbing 0.16 % a minute. Duty pump P-103 shows no run feedback at CP-402; standby P-104 is on manual start. V-504 suction valve was last seen open.

turns.speaker: bristol-compliance
turns.text: W-1201 is a public route. Floors and traffic routes must be kept free of anything that makes people slip, so close it to visitors before the water reaches the lip, and log the closure.

turns.speaker: bristol-technician
turns.text: I can reach {contactName} ({contactRole}) by {contactChannel} through the dispatch line now; the visitor operations lead has no contact details on file, so the closure notice is recorded for the log.

records.resolution: Close W-1201 to visitors now; {contactName} attends to start standby pump P-104 at CP-402 and check P-103; compliance logs the walkway closure.

summary.headline: SU-201 at {value} %: close W-1201, start P-104

P-103 shows no run feedback; P-104 is on manual start.
decisions: Close the visitor walkway W-1201 now.
{contactName} starts P-104 and checks P-103.

Log the walkway closure

turns.speaker: bristol-manager
turns.text: Call convened on PV-301: the examination certificate has expired and the public steam demonstration depends on it. Compliance first.

turns.speaker: bristol-compliance
turns.text: BR-WSE-PV301-2025 expired 2 days ago. Under the Pressure Systems Safety Regulations a pressure system must not be operated after the date its written-scheme examination was due, so PV-301 cannot be steamed for the public until it is re-examined.

turns.speaker: bristol-engineer
turns.text: PV-301 is cold and isolated at V-501. V-505's lift test is due with the same examination, so one competent-person visit clears both.

records.resolution: The public steam demonstration stays blocked; {contactName} ({contactRole}) books the competent person and confirms the cancellation; compliance sends the site engineer the expired certificate for the file.

V-505's lift test falls due with the same examination.
decisions: Keep the public steam demonstration blocked.
Book one competent-person visit for PV-301 and V-505.

actions.task: Book the competent person and confirm the cancellation
Email the expired certificate to the site engineer

turns.speaker: tomioka-engineer
turns.text: Site Manager, HS-301 reads {value} % RH in the Silk Reeling Mill and is still rising after the typhoon. Above 65 % for long, mould starts on the king-post trusses TR-201 to TR-204 and on the reeling machines. I want DH-1101 running and the north windows closed now.

turns.speaker: tomioka-manager
turns.text: Agreed. Compliance, what does this mean for us as the owner of designated buildings?

turns.speaker: tomioka-compliance
turns.text: As the owner of National Treasure buildings we must manage them properly under the Act on Protection of Cultural Properties (art. 31, 第31条, applied to the Historic Site by art. 119), and damage to them has to be reported (art. 33, 第33条). Keeping the hall dry is part of that duty, so we log every reading until it is back under 65 %.

turns.speaker: tomioka-manager
turns.text: Technician, send Kobayashi Mio, our conservator, to start DH-1101 and close the north windows.

turns.speaker: tomioka-technician
turns.text: Sending the conservator through the dispatch line now. She is synthetic crew with no contact on file, so the request is recorded for the log; I will report when DH-1101 is running.

summary.headline: HS-301 at {value} % RH: start DH-1101, close the north windows
points: HS-301 rose from 79.6 to {value} % RH after the typhoon against a 65 % preservation limit.
Mould risk to trusses TR-201 to TR-204 and the reeling machines.
Managing the National Treasure buildings is the owner's duty (Act on Protection of Cultural Properties art. 31).
decisions: Start DH-1101 and close the north windows.
Log HS-301 to HS-303 hourly until under 65 %.

turns.speaker: tomioka-manager
turns.text: Meeting on TM-WO-2026-117: the contractor wants to drill four anchors into BW-251 for the new humidity sensors. Compliance first.

turns.speaker: tomioka-compliance
turns.text: BW-251 is National Treasure fabric. Drilling anchors alters its current state, which needs the Commissioner for Cultural Affairs' permission under the Act on Protection of Cultural Properties (art. 43, 第43条); doing it without permission is an offence (art. 197). turns.text: The new sensors weigh under a kilogram. Padded clamps on free-standing posts hold them without touching the brick, and the cables can follow the existing route except for one new entry through the wall.

turns.speaker: tomioka-technician
turns.text: I can tell {contactName} ({contactRole}) through the dispatch line; synthetic crew have no contact on file, so the request is recorded for the log.

records.resolution: No drilling into BW-251: the contractor fits non-invasive clamp mounts on free-standing posts; {contactName} ({contactRole}) prepares the permission request for the one new cable entry; the work order is revised.

summary.headline: TM-WO-2026-117 blocked: clamp mounts instead of drilling BW-251

Clamp mounts on free-standing posts touch no historic fabric.
decisions: Revise the work order to non-invasive clamp mounts.
File the permission request for the cable entry.

records.topic: Heritage-safe sensor mounting and route closure

turns.speaker: tomioka-compliance
turns.text: Tomioka here. We cannot drill National Treasure fabric for our new humidity sensors without the Commissioner's permission. How do you mount sensors on your 1907 pumps without altering the historic metalwork, and how do you close a visitor route during a hazard?

turns.speaker: bristol-compliance
turns.text: Padded stainless clamps on existing frame members: no drilling, welding or adhesive, and every mount photographed and logged; cables stay in existing conduits. For a hazard we close W-1201 at its entrance with the barrier and sign, sweep the route, log the time and reason, and reopen only after the visitor lead walks it: a traffic route must stay free of slip hazards (Workplace Regulations reg 12) and visitors must not be put at risk (HSWA s 3). I will email our method statement.

turns.speaker: tomioka-compliance
turns.text: Thank you. We will adapt both to our rules: alterations here need permission under art. 43, and our route closure has to fit the fire defence plan. I will ask our Site Manager to agree it with your Plant Manager.

summary.headline: Bristol shares its clamp-mount method and route-closure procedure
points: Bristol clamps sensors to existing frame members with no drilling, welding or adhesive.
Bristol closes W-1201 with a barrier, a sweep and a logged reopening walk-through.
decisions: Adapt Bristol's method and procedure for Tomioka.

actions.task: Email the heritage method statement
Agree a shared installation window with Bristol
